Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 4b) shows a distinct retrocardiac tubular opacity (indicated by arrows) representing an anomalous systemic artery supplying the left lower lobe, which is the hallmark radiographic sign of systemic arterialization of the lung without sequestration (also known as Pryce type I sequestration or anomalous systemic arterial supply). Unlike classic bronchopulmonary sequestration, this condition typically lacks a discrete cystic or solid mass in the lung parenchyma.
